directives.trigger: One or more files are in hand and the ask is what is this: format, class, endianness, architecture, entry. Quiet for function lists, call graphs, naming, lifting, or decrypting or bypassing anything.
directives.doneWhen: `python3 fixtures/re-triage/check.py --fixture <dir> --out <out.json>` exits 0: for each file the output fields format, class, endian, arch, and entry (the entry point address) equal what the checker parses from `file` and `readelf -h` itself, or is {"stop":"tools disagree"} when the tools error or disagree, or {"unsupported":"not ELF"}.
directives.forbidden: any field the tools did not emit; continuing past a disagreement; anything beyond identification (no decryption, no bypass)

directives.trigger: A binary is in hand and triage already named its format and architecture; the ask is the function list, call graph, or strings. Quiet for names or purposes, runtime behavior, or decrypting or bypassing.
directives.doneWhen: One combined output holding the function list, the call-graph edge list, and the strings is generated from `objdump -d` and `strings` output twice, and `cmp first.out second.out` exits 0 (all three regenerate byte for byte). A binary with no functions is a valid result: empty function and edge sections that regenerate empty, not a guess.
directives.forbidden: redrawing or editing the call graph by hand or by model; adding an edge or function the disassembler output does not show; listing any function address or string the tool output does not contain
absentTools: headless disassembler with a call-graph export

directives.trigger: A known-architecture sample with ground truth exists and a target needs a recovered spec. Quiet when no scored sample exists, or for decrypting or bypassing.
directives.doneWhen: A scoring program run on the known-architecture sample prints the line "lift: M/N matched" and exits 0, and writes remainder.json holding exactly N-M items (the unmatched ones; `jq length remainder.json` equals N-M), which is the only input a model pass receives. M=N (empty remainder), or an unknown architecture reported as "unsupported", is a valid result.
directives.forbidden: sending the whole target, or any item outside remainder.json, to a model; touching the target before the known-architecture score exists; calling an unknown-ISA lift reliable

directives.trigger: A static claim list and a saved emulation trace are both in hand. Quiet when only one exists, to start hardware, or to decrypt or bypass anything.
directives.doneWhen: A comparison program prints "claims: K kept, D dropped of N" with K+D=N; each dropped claim cites the contradicting trace line by line number and no kept claim has one. With no trace the result is "unsupported: no trace" and exit 0.
directives.forbidden: keeping a claim the trace contradicts, or dropping one without a cited trace line; inventing a trace when no emulator is registered

directives.trigger: Saved captures are in hand and the ask is to parse them and show the parse reproduces them. Quiet for live interception, crafting or replaying traffic, or decrypting or bypassing.
directives.doneWhen: For every capture, parse then re-serialize, and `cmp capture.bin roundtrip.bin` exits 0. A capture that does not round-trip is reported as failed, and an empty capture set is a valid result.
directives.forbidden: parsing any field not seen in the captures in hand; generalizing a field layout, length rule, or message type past the captures in hand; calling a spec from a few captures trustworthy

directives.trigger: A function from disassembly or decompilation needs a name or one-line purpose. Quiet when the ask is only listing functions, or decrypting or bypassing anything.
directives.doneWhen: Each proposed name carries a quoted evidence line: a string with its offset, a call target with its address, or a trace line with its line number, confirmed by a program to appear in the tool output at that locator. A function with no evidence stays unnamed, a valid result. This proves the evidence exists, not that the name is right.
directives.forbidden: giving a plausible name with no string, call, or trace behind it

directives.trigger: Findings from any reverse-engineering directive exist, or a session must resume one. Quiet when there is nothing yet to record.
directives.doneWhen: A fresh session reads only the state file and its listed artifacts and writes restated.json; then `jq -S .findings state.json > a.json; jq -S .findings restated.json > b.json; cmp a.json b.json` exits 0 (the resumed findings equal the saved findings). An empty findings list is a valid result.
directives.forbidden: leaving findings in chat only, or resuming from memory instead of the files
